subject: Model-fit evals & structured-output follow-up — Acme Corp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme-corp.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T15:00:00-07:00
Subject: Model-fit evals & structured-output follow-up — Acme Corp

Thanks for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Key takeaways:
- Primary goal: reliably extract structured invoice data (JSON schema) and surface a short confidence score for downstream routing.
- Volume: ~10k requests/day; critical path latency target is 95th pct <= 350ms.
- Acceptance criteria: schema compliance >= 98% (after retries / post-processing) for production.
- Current concerns: some fields (tax_amount, vendor_id) are prone to hallucination when prompts are ambiguous.

Recommended experiment (baseline):
1) Run a 1k-sample evaluation using our structured-output harness (attached prompt set: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv).
2) Models to test: redwood-v1-medium-quant (fast, good cost/latency), redwood-v1-small-quant (low-cost baseline), and open-llama-13b (control).
3) Eval metrics: JSON Schema pass-rate, field-level precision/recall, avg token cost, 95th pct latency.
4) Function-calling configuration: temperature=0.0, deterministic sampling, max_retries_on_schema_fail=2.

Deliverables / timeline:
- We can spin up a 1k evaluation and initial report within 3 business days.
- Follow-up deep-dive (30m) to review results and agree on pilot configuration.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.csv, eval_results_summary_20260915.pdf (sample), eval-harness-config.yaml

Next steps for you:
- Confirm you want us to run the 1k eval against the attached prompts.
- Share any forbidden fields or extra validation rules (e.g., vendor_id must match your vendor registry).

Thanks — I'll loop Dev and Rishi to own the evaluation run once you confirm.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme-corp.com>

Date: 2026-09-15T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit evals & structured-output follow-up — Acme Corp

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick Qs before we greenlight the run: 

On Sep 15, 2026, at 3:00 PM, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Primary goal: reliably extract structured invoice data (JSON schema) and surface a short confidence score for downstream routing.

1) Latency: you flagged 95th pct <=350ms as our target — is that achievable for redwood-v1-medium-quant at our volume without Dedicated?
2) Schema pass-rate: you suggested >=98% after retries. What's the typical out-of-the-box pass rate we should expect before prompt tuning / post-processing?
3) If we see persistent failures on vendor_id, can we call an external vendor-lookup microservice as a post-step (we'd need guidance on secure function-calling setup)?

If answers to 1-3 look reasonable I'm happy to approve the 1k run. Also propose a 30m technical call with Dev + Rishi (next Tue/Wed) to cover the function-calling integration and security constraints.

—
Jordan Liu
Product Manager, Payments
Acme Corp
jordan.liu@acme-corp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme-corp.com>, Samir Shah <samir.shah@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit evals & structured-output follow-up — Acme Corp

Great questions — short answers: 
1) Latency: For hosted/shared capacity we typically see redwood-v1-medium-quant hit 95th pct ~250-400ms depending on seq length; for stable 95th pct <=350ms at your 10k/day profile we recommend Dedicated or reserved bursts during pilot. We'll include latency breakdown in the report.
2) Schema pass-rate: out-of-the-box function-calling pass-rates vary; our historical baseline on invoice-style tasks is ~88-93% (no retries). With prompt templates + 1 automatic retry on schema failure you often reach ~96-98%. Post-processing validators (simple field coersion + vendor lookup) regularly push that to >=99%.
3) External lookup: yes — function-calling to a vendor-lookup API is a standard pattern. We can provide a secure, signed webhook pattern and example adapter. For pilot we can simulate the lookup (no access to your registry) and show the improvement in compliance.

I've tentatively scheduled a 30m technical call Wed 2026-09-22 10:00am PT with our solutions team (please confirm). If that works, Dev and Rishi will run the 1k eval immediately after the call and share the Drive report link.

Action: Jordan — please confirm the call time and any field-level rules (e.g., vendor_id regex, allowed currencies).

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-09-16T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model-fit evals & structured-output follow-up — Acme Corp

Looping in the technical plan so everyone has visibility. We'll run the structured-output eval harness against the attached prompt set and the following config: 

- Models: redwood-v1-medium-quant, redwood-v1-small-quant, open-llama-13b
- Sampling: temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0
- Retries: max_attempts_on_schema_fail = 2 (immediate retry with tighter prompt)
- Post-processing: JSON Schema validator (ajv), field-level normalization (numbers, currency), optional vendor-lookup hook (mocked for pilot)
- Eval size: 1,000 prompts (random stratified by seq length)
- Metrics: schema_pass_rate_before_retries, schema_pass_rate_after_retries, field_precision_recall, avg_token_cost, p95_latency

Deliverables: 
1) Upload full run artifacts (raw outputs + validation logs) to Drive and link in HubSpot.
2) Short executive summary PDF (eval_results_summary_20260915.pdf already shows sample layout).
3) If we see vendor_id failures >2% after retries we'll enable the vendor-lookup hook and re-run a 500-sample follow-up.

Security note: function-calling / webhook patterns will use signed requests and short-lived tokens; we'll provide example adapter code and a runbook for you.

I'll start the run once Jordan confirms the call and any additional field rules. Expect initial results within 72 hours of run start.

—
